summary:
The “Preventing the Financing of Illegal Synthetic Drugs Act” (Public Law 118-79) directs the Comptroller General of the United States to conduct a study and issue a report on illicit finance connected to the trafficking of synthetic drugs. The Act does not amend existing statutory law, authorize appropriations, or create new regulatory authorities; it imposes a single, time-limited study and reporting obligation on the Government Accountability Office.

Section 3(a) mandates that the Comptroller General “shall carry out a study on illicit financing in connection with the trafficking of synthetic drugs,” enumerating specific substances: fentanyl, methamphetamine, fentanyl- and methamphetamine-related substances, Captagon, and fentanyl and methamphetamine precursors. The study must examine seven categories of information: (1) the business of synthetic drug trafficking and related illicit finance, including the role of transnational criminal organizations and terror syndicates and their trafficking corridors, source countries, and transit countries; (2) the business models of such organizations, encompassing precursor acquisition or production, supply-chain movement, manufacture, marketing, distribution, sales, and repatriation of proceeds; (3) the overlap between human trafficking business models and synthetic drug trafficking and related illicit finance; (4) the use of online illicit drug markets and social media for marketing, sale, and payment; (5) financial methods used by these organizations, specifically payment, money laundering, and repatriation of proceeds; (6) the use of social media applications and payment applications (identified as Snap Chat, Discord, Facebook, and CashApp) to facilitate financial transactions for synthetic drug trafficking, particularly among young people; and (7) U.S. Government activities to combat such illicit finance, including interagency, intergovernmental, and private-sector collaboration, as well as identified gaps or resource deficiencies in those coordination efforts.

Section 3(b) requires the Comptroller General, not later than one year after the date of enactment (enacted September 13, 2024), to “issue a report to the Congress containing all findings and determinations made in carrying out the study required under subsection (a).”

Sections 1 and 2 consist of the short title and a non-operative findings section, respectively. The Act contains no appropriations, authorizations of appropriations, sunset provisions, or delegation of rulemaking authority. The sole operative requirement is the production of the study and report within the prescribed deadline.
